summary: Both editions were independently checked against all four paragraphs of the selected Greek working source. Both preserve the infant comparison, negations, reason for dwelling in God’s kingdom, comparative honor and priority, moral-change language, speakers, and stone categories. Their notes accurately identify the marked portions and disclose that their precise editorial status remains unresolved; they do not certify those portions as preserved manuscript text. The supplied apparatus excerpt does not resolve those marks in section xxix, and the reported Greek/Latin boundary and Amherst evidence concern section xxx, not this unit. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Acceptance is limited to the supplied working source and disclosures, not unseen manuscripts, edition authentication, or exhaustive collation.
